Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-8", "title": "Stroke", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "A stroke happens when there is a loss of blood flow to part of the brain."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your brain cells cannot get the oxygen and nutrients they need from blood, and they start to die within a few minutes."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This can cause lasting brain damage, long-term disability, or even death."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "If you think that you or someone else is having a stroke, call 911 right away."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Immediate treatment may save someone's life and increase the chances for successful rehabilitation and recovery."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "There are two types of stroke: Ischemic stroke is caused by a blood clot that blocks or plugs a blood vessel in the brain."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This is the most common type; about 80% of strokes are ischemic."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Hemorrhagic stroke is caused by a blood vessel that breaks and bleeds into the brain."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Another condition that's similar to a stroke is a transient ischemic attack (TIA)."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It's sometimes called a \"mini-stroke.\" TIAs happen when the blood supply to the brain is blocked for a short time."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The damage to the brain cells isn't permanent, but having a TIA puts you at much higher risk of having a stroke."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Certain factors can raise your risk of a stroke."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The major risk factors include: High blood pressure ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "This is the primary risk factor for a stroke."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Atrial fibrillation and other heart diseases can cause blood clots that lead to stroke."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "When you smoke, you damage your blood vessels and raise your blood pressure."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "A personal or family history of stroke or TIA Age."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Your risk of stroke increases as you get older."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "People who are African American or Hispanic have a higher risk of stroke."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "There are also other factors that are linked to a higher risk of stroke, such as: Alcohol and illegal drug use Not getting enough physical activity High cholesterol Unhealthy diet Having obesity What are the symptoms of a stroke?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The symptoms of a stroke often happen quickly."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "They include: Sudden numbness or weakness of the face, arm, or leg (especially on one side of the body) Sudden confusion, trouble speaking, or understanding speech Sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes Sudden difficulty walking, dizziness, loss of balance or coordination Sudden severe headache with no known cause The F.A.S.T."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "test can help you remember what to look for if you think someone is having a stroke."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Think \"FAST\" and look for: F ace drooping on one side when smiling."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "A rm weakness occurs when the arms are raised, and one arm drifts downward."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "If you think that you or someone else is having a stroke, call 911 right away."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "To make a diagnosis, your health care provider will: Ask about your symptoms and medical history Do a physical exam, including a check of: Your mental alertness Your coordination and balance Any numbness or weakness in your face, arms, and legs Any trouble speaking and seeing clearly Run some tests, which may include: Diagnostic imaging of the brain, such as a CT scan or MRI ."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Heart tests , which can help detect heart problems or blood clots that may have led to a stroke."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Possible tests include an electrocardiogram (EKG) and an echocardiography."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Treatments for stroke include medicines, surgery, and rehabilitation."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Which treatments you get depend on the type of stroke and the stage of treatment."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "The different stages are: Acute treatment , to try to stop a stroke while it is happening Post-stroke rehabilitation , to overcome the disabilities caused by the stroke Prevention , to prevent a first stroke or, if you have already had one, prevent another stroke Acute treatments for ischemic stroke are usually medicines: You may get tPA, (tissue plasminogen activator), a medicine to dissolve the blood clot."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "You can only get this medicine within 4 hours of when your symptoms started."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "The sooner you can get it, the better your chance of recovery."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "If you cannot get that medicine, you may get medicine that helps stop platelets from clumping together to form blood clots."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Or you may get a blood thinner to keep existing clots from getting bigger."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "If you have carotid artery disease, you may also need a procedure to open your blocked carotid artery."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Acute treatments for hemorrhagic stroke focus on stopping the bleeding."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "The first step is to find the cause of bleeding in the brain."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "The next step is to control it: If high blood pressure is the cause of bleeding, you may be given blood pressure medicines ."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "If an aneurysm is the cause, you may need aneurysm clipping or coil embolization."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "These are surgeries to prevent further leaking of blood from the aneurysm."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "They also can help prevent the aneurysm from bursting again."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "If an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) is the cause of a stroke, you may need an AVM repair."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "An AVM is a tangle of faulty arteries and veins that can rupture within the brain."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "An AVM repair may be done through: Surgery Injecting a substance into the blood vessels of the AVM to block blood flow Radiation to shrink the blood vessels of the AVM Stroke rehabilitation can help you relearn skills you lost because of the damage."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "The goal is to help you become as independent as possible and have the best possible quality of life."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Prevention of another stroke is also important, since having a stroke increases the risk of getting another one."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Prevention may include heart-healthy lifestyle changes and medicines."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "If you have already had a stroke or are at risk of having a stroke, you can make some heart-healthy lifestyle changes to try to prevent a future stroke: Eating a heart-healthy diet Aiming for a healthy weight Managing stress Getting regular physical activity Quitting smoking Managing your blood pressure and cholesterol levels If these changes aren't enough, you may need medicine to control your risk factors."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-4272", "title": "Rett Syndrome", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Rett syndrome is a rare genetic disease that causes developmental and nervous system problems, mostly in girls."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It's related to autism spectrum disorder ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Babies with Rett syndrome seem to grow and develop normally at first."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Between 3 months and 3 years of age, though, they stop developing and even lose some skills."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Symptoms include: Loss of speech Loss of hand movements such as grasping Compulsive movements such as hand wringing Balance problems Breathing problems Behavior problems Learning problems or intellectual disability Rett syndrome has no cure."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You can treat some of the symptoms with medicines, surgery, and physical and speech therapy."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Most people with Rett syndrome live into middle age and beyond."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "They will usually need care throughout their lives."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development"}]}, {"id": "MLP-176", "title": "Burns", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "A burn is damage to your body's tissues caused by heat, chemicals, electricity , sunlight , or radiation ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Scalds from hot liquids and steam, building fires and flammable liquids and gases are the most common causes of burns."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Another kind is an inhalation injury , caused by breathing smoke."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are three types of burns: First-degree burns damage only the outer layer of skin Second-degree burns damage the outer layer and the layer underneath Third-degree burns damage or destroy the deepest layer of skin and tissues underneath Burns can cause swelling, blistering, scarring and, in serious cases, shock , and even death."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "They also can lead to infections because they damage your skin's protective barrier."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Treatment for burns depends on the cause of the burn, how deep it is, and how much of the body it covers."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Antibiotic creams can prevent or treat infections."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "For more serious burns, treatment may be needed to clean the wound, replace the skin, and make sure the patient has enough fluids and nutrition."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "NIH: National Institute of General Medical Sciences"}]}, {"id": "MLP-4604", "title": "Wildfires", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Wildfires are fires that burn out of control in a natural area, like a forest, grassland, or prairie."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They spread quickly, and can damage natural resources, destroy homes, and threaten the safety of the public and firefighters."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can be an accident, like when people don't take care of their campfire properly, burn debris, or are careless when getting rid of their cigarettes."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It can also be on purpose, which is called arson."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Lightning and lava also can also cause wildfires."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Wildfires are more common when conditions are dry."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "High winds can make them spread more quickly."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Although there are no guarantees of safety if you live in an area threatened by a wildfire, you can take actions to protect yourself."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Being prepared can help reduce fear, anxiety, and losses."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "If you do experience a disaster, it is normal to feel stressed."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "You may need help in finding ways to cope ."}]}, {"id": "MLP-198", "title": "Congenital Heart Defects", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are problems with the structure of the heart."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "\"Congenital\" means that that the problems are present at birth."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "These defects happen when a fetus's heart doesn't develop normally during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Congenital heart defects are the most common type of birth defect ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Congenital heart defects can change the way the heart pumps blood."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "They may make blood flow too slowly, go the wrong way, or block it completely."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There are many types of congenital heart defects."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "They can happen in one or more parts of the heart."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The most common types are: Septal defects (\"hole in the heart\") - openings in the wall between the left and right sides of the heart Heart valve defects - problems with the valves that control the flow of blood through the heart Defects in the large blood vessels that carry blood in and out of the heart Congenital heart defects can range from very mild problems that never need treatment to life-threatening problems at birth."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The most serious congenital heart defects are called critical congenital heart disease ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Babies with these defects usually need surgery in the first year of life."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But the symptoms of milder heart defects may not show up until childhood or adulthood."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Researchers often don't know what causes congenital heart defects."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "They do know that changes in a baby's genes sometimes cause a heart defect."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The changed genes may come from the parents, or the changes may happen during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Who is more likely to have a baby with a congenital heart defect?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Several things may increase the chance that your baby has a congenital heart defect, such as: Your health before and during pregnancy , including: Having diabetes before pregnancy or developing it in the first 3 months of pregnancy (diabetes that develops later in pregnancy isn't a major risk for heart defects)."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Carefully controlling your blood glucose , also called blood sugar, before and during pregnancy can lower your baby's risk of congenital heart defects."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Having phenylketonuria (PKU), a rare inherited disorder that affects how the body uses a protein in foods."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "If you have PKU, eating a low-protein diet before getting pregnant can lower your baby's risk of having a congenital heart defect."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Having rubella (German measles) during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Your contact with certain substances during pregnancy , including: Smoking or secondhand smoke (breathing smoke from another smoker)."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Certain medicines , such as angiotensin-converting (ACE) inhibitors for high blood pressure and retinoic acids for acne."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "If you're pregnant or plan to get pregnant, talk with your health care provider about all the medicines you take."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "In most cases, congenital heart defects don't run in families."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But your chance of having a baby with a congenital heart defect does go up if you or the other parent has a congenital heart defect, or if you already have a child with a congenital heart defect."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "What are the symptoms of congenital heart defects?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Congenital heart defects don't cause pain."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "The signs and symptoms are different, depending on the type and number of defects and how serious they are."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Common signs and symptoms of congenital heart defects include: Cyanosis - a bluish color to the skin, lips, and fingernails."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "It happens when there isn't enough oxygen in the blood."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Fatigue - your baby may be unusually sleepy and may become very tired during feedings."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Heart murmur - an unusual sound between heartbeats."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "What other problems do congenital heart defects cause?"}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Congenital heart defects don't always cause other problems."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "If they do, which problems you have would depend on the type and number of defects and how serious the defects are."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Children with congenital heart defects are more likely to: Be smaller than other children Have problems or delays in mental, and emotional growth, and behavior, such as: Speech and language problems Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) People with congenital heart defects may develop other health conditions, including: Endocarditis - an infection of lining of the heart and valves Arrhythmia - a problem with the rate or rhythm of your heartbeat Heart failure - when your heart can't pump enough blood to the body Pulmonary hypertension - high blood pressure in your lungs Kidney and liver disease How are congenital heart defects diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Before a baby is born , your provider may use ultrasound pictures of the fetus's heart to look for heart defects."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "It's done between weeks 18 and 22 of pregnancy."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "During the first few days after birth , all newborns are checked for congenital heart defects."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "A pulse oximeter is clipped to your baby's hands or feet to measure blood oxygen."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "If it shows low levels of blood oxygen, more tests will be needed to find out if your baby has a heart defect."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "To diagnose congenital heart defects in babies, children, and adults , a provider may use many tools, including: A physical exam."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Certain heart tests to see how the heart is working."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Genetic testing to see if certain gene problems caused the defect."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "What are the treatments for congenital heart defects?"}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Treatment depends on the type of congenital heart defect and how serious it is."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Possible treatments include: Cardiac catheterization to repair simple defects, such as a small hole in the inside wall of the heart."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "A catheterization uses a thin tube guided through a vein and into the heart."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Heart surgery may be needed to: Repair defects in the heart and blood vessels."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Place a device in the chest to help the heart pump blood."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Do a heart transplant Medicine is often used if your baby has a specific type of congenital heart defect called patent ductus arteriosus."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "All children and adults who have congenital heart defects need regular follow-up care from a cardiologist (a doctor who specializes in heart diseases) throughout their life, even if their defect was repaired."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "Some people may need several heart surgeries or catheterizations over the years."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "They may also need to take medicines to help their hearts work as well as possible."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}]
